q: A goose recipe YAML's run-time inputs live in which block?
options: parameters — keys with defaults that the prompt interpolates as {{ key }}
extensions — which are substituted at parse time
activities — one value per input
title — serialized as env vars
explanation: extensions declare allowed tooling, not inputs.
activities list capabilities, not parameter values.
title is a display string; no env serialization happens.

q: `goose run` prints the cli.rs:2244 error when:
options: None of --instructions, --text, or --recipe was provided
The recipe file contains a parameter without a default
The binary was built with debug symbols
A provider API key is missing
explanation: A missing default is a recipe-authoring gap, not a CLI usage error.
Debug builds are fully supported for runs.
Key errors surface later, from the provider, not as this usage error.

q: Phase guards in the self-test prompt use `{% if test_phases == "all" or "basic" in test_phases %}` to:
options: Run a phase only when its name is selected, so bounded runs skip unrelated scenarios
Encrypt the phase block from casual readers
Guarantee phases run in parallel
Validate YAML syntax at load time
explanation: There is no encryption semantics in recipe templates.
Parallelism is controlled elsewhere (parallel_tests parameter).
The guard is about conditional inclusion, not syntax validation.

q: The nested-delegation scenario is CRITICAL in the self-test suite because:
options: A delegate spawning delegates would bypass SessionType::SubAgent recursion prevention — a security boundary
It consumes the most tokens of any scenario
Delegates are the newest extension type
It only runs on release branches
explanation: Cost is not the criterion for CRITICAL severity.
Age of a feature doesn't determine test severity.
The suite runs anywhere; severity comes from what the check enforces.

options: The recipe can reference its own bundled script by relative path wherever the recipe lives
The recipe can upload itself to the workspace root
Recipes can hard-code absolute Linux paths on all platforms
The prompt can switch working directories mid-run
explanation: No upload behavior exists in recipe templating.
Hard-coded absolute paths would break portability — the opposite of the mechanism.
Directory switching is shell behavior, not a template variable.

q: You ran the recipe without rebuilding after your change, and the run still passed. The correct conclusion is:
options: The run did NOT validate your change — the binary predates it, so rebuild and rerun
The recipe run is smarter than the compiled binary
Recipes validate source files directly
The change needs no validation since tests were green
explanation: Recipes drive the compiled binary as-is; there is no intelligence layer above it.
The prompt watches observable behavior, not source text.
The whole point of the recipe run is end-to-end validation of the built artifact.

q: Fix this recipe authoring failure: your new scenario runs on every phase selection but its log path `{{ workspace_dir }}/phase_label_fitting.md` is only created in some branches. The fix:
options: Move the log write inside the same guarded block that runs the scenario, so selection and artifact always match
Create the file unconditionally at recipe load
Remove the workspace_dir parameter entirely
Rename the file to a global path outside workspace_dir
explanation: Creating artifacts unconditionally misstates what actually ran — the report lies by omission.
workspace_dir scoping is what keeps the archive phase working; removal breaks cleanup.
Leaving the workspace breaks the recipe's own archive/cleanup contract.
